newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan govt, rebel troops reported in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Angolan govt, rebel troops reported in Zaire.

text.p: Angolan government soldiers and former UNITA rebels have moved into Zaire in recent weeks with at least some involved in the fighting in the east of the country, a United Nations source and diplomats said on Tuesday.
"We have seen troop movements on both sides into Zaire," said a U.N. official who asked not be identified.

The official said UNITA troops had been flown out of bases in UNITA-held territory at Lusamba and Jamba to help the government of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko in its fight against Tutsi-led rebels.
"We think at least 2,000 UNITA troops have been sent to Zaire. Most of these are fighting troops," the U.N. source said.
He said UNITA had become involved in the conflict, which has raged since last October, in a bid to keep open vital supply routes out of Zaire to its bases in the north and east of Angola.
The role of Angolan government soldiers was not as clear but sources said technical advisors had been sent to assist the Zairean rebels amid hopes of cutting off the UNITA supplies.
However, diplomatic sources in Luanda said UNITA involvement in the fighting had recently stopped because the Angolans were suffering too many casualties.
"UNITA went off to Zaire but soon found they were doing most of the fighting...they went up there to help Mobutu, not to fight this war for him," a diplomat who asked not to be identified said.

U.N. and other sources also said the Angolan government has started the mass movement of Katangese combatants, veterans of failed secessionist wars in the southern Zaire province of Shaba in the 1970s and 1980s, back to Zaire.

Katangese troops, some regular members of the Angolan military, together with arms have been flown to the Rwandan capital Kigali and then on to Goma in eastern Zaire. They are apparently helping the rebels trying to overthrow Mobutu.
International pressure has recently mounted on the Angolan government and UNITA not to meddle in the Zairean conflict amid signs the war is spreading and threatening to suck in its neighbours.
UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi recently denied military involvement in Zaire. Angolan military officials were on Tuesday unavailable for comment but in the past have also denied troop activity.
